subject: APAC + EU Edge RetryStorm & Proxy Saturation — urgent
body:
-----Original Message-----
From: Samantha Liu <samantha@aurora-payments.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@aurora-payments.com
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike: 502/503 errors in APAC + EU — urgent

Hi Aditya,

We started seeing elevated 502/503 and client-side timeouts around 08:45 UTC in both APAC and EU regions. Our payments processing jobs are getting intermittent 502 responses and many clients are retrying aggressively — our telemetry shows a retry amplification pattern that correlates with your edge returning 502/503/504 at ~5xx rate ~12% for the past 20 minutes. We’re seeing end-user timeouts and some abandoned transactions.

I attached a sampled log and a CSV with request rates. Can you confirm if there’s an in-flight incident on Redwood’s side or if this looks like a client retry storm on our end? This is high-severity for our customers.

— Samantha
Samantha Liu
Head of Platform, Aurora Payments

-----Reply (internal)-----
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Liu <samantha@aurora-payments.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike: 502/503 errors in APAC + EU — urgent

Thanks for flagging, Samantha — we see the same signal in our edge telemetry. Root cause isn’t fully nailed yet but early correlates: sudden surge in short-lived connections from Aurora’s public endpoints + client retries -> proxy queue saturation -> backend connection resets returning 502/503.

Immediate actions we’ve kicked off:
- Routed traffic away from the most hit frontends to spare capacity pools (APAC eu-west-1 and eu-central-2)
- Throttled excessive connection bursts at the LB layer (soft cap) to keep proxies healthy
- Opened a dedicated trace for Aurora’s requests (trace ids appended in attachment sample)

Can the Aurora ops team share client retry settings (backoff jitter, max attempts)? That will help determine whether throttling or a temporary config change is necessary. I’ll loop infra for queue-depth tuning.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Regional Sales — APAC, Redwood Inference

-----Quoted: Samantha's reply-----

-----Internal escalation to Execs & Infra-----
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Liu <samantha@aurora-payments.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Spike: 502/503 errors in APAC + EU — urgent

Looping infra and support leadership. Customer is P1 for us (Aurora). Need a quick mitigation plan and a customer note. Also flagging this for potential SLA credit discussion depending on duration.

Proposed mitigations (prioritized):
1) Short window routing to Dedicated pool for Aurora (can we carve a hot path for 30m?) — Marcus, can you confirm capacity?
2) Increase proxy worker threads and increase per-proxy conn limit temporarily to reduce 502s from queue drops
3) Enforce a per-client 429 throttle at the edge (soft 5s window) so backend isn’t hammered by aggressive retries
4) Patch quick telemetry to expose per-origin queue depth and retry count for customer-facing dashboard

We need:
- ETA for routing change (aditya + marcus)
- One-line customer update by 10:15 PST (aditya)

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

-----Infra reply (technical)-----
From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Liu <samantha@aurora-payments.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike: 502/503 errors in APAC + EU — urgent

Summary of findings so far:
- Metrics: APAC edge queue depth spiked to 380% of baseline; 5xx rate at egress proxies peaked 14% for 5m windows.
- Upstream failures: backends remained healthy, low CPU/RPS on inference fleet; failures originate at proxy handoff (timeouts and RST).
- Likely amplifier: client retry policy with no jitter and short retry windows causing synchronized bursts.

Immediate mitigations applied (10:05 PST):
- Enabled short-lived per-origin 429 throttling (soft limit: 100rps aggregated per origin; 95th percentile relaxed after 20m)
- Increased proxy accept queue and worker threads (rolling across affected frontends)
- Temporarily routed Aurora VIP traffic to an underutilized dedicated pool in APAC for 45 minutes

Remaining asks:
- Request Aurora to push backoff patch (recommended exponential backoff with jitter, max attempts 4)
- Confirm whether Partner integration (Acme) was also sending bursts — I see overlapping IPs in the logs.

Working on a post-mortem ticket and will attach metric graphs once available.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
SRE — Traffic & Edge, Redwood Inference

-----Customer acknowledgement and short update-----
From: Samantha Liu <samantha@aurora-payments.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike: 502/503 errors in APAC + EU — urgent

Thanks — we’ve applied a client-side emergency throttle (max attempts=3, 500ms jitter) and see errors decline in APAC within ~6 minutes. EU still has elevated 5xx for some endpoints, looks like a downstream gateway timed out intermittently.

Please confirm when the dedicated routing ends and whether we should expect follow-up maintenance.

— Samantha

-----Final internal note and exec ask (18:45)-----
From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Liu <samantha@aurora-payments.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 18:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike: 502/503 errors in APAC + EU — urgent

Status: incident mitigated; residual 5xx in EU reduced to <1%. Customer reports improved success rates post-edge throttling and client patch.

Action items for follow-up:
- Post-mortem with Aurora & Acme teams; include timeline and exact traffic samples (Marcus)
- Update SLA/credits calculation if customer impact window > 30m (Laura + Finance)
- Engineering: implement per-origin health signals and a circuit-breaker that opens before proxy queue saturates (P2)
- Sales: coordinate a customer communication and potential credits request if they escalate to their leadership (Aditya)

Customer-facing summary (send ASAP):
> We observed a client-driven retry amplification combined with short proxy queue limits in APAC and EU. We implemented temporary routing and edge throttling and recommend Aurora patch their client retry logic (exponential backoff + jitter, max attempts=4). We will follow up with a detailed post-mortem and any SLA guidance.

— Sean Gallagher
VP, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
